provenance.quote: HOVILPRI is a herpes simplex virus (HSV) helicase-primase inhibitor indicated

sections.title: Mechanism of Action
sections.text: HOVILPRI is an antiviral drug against HSV-1 and HSV-2 [see Microbiology (12.4)].

sections.title: Pharmacodynamics
sections.text: Exposure-Response No exposure-response relationship was identified between steady-state plasma pritelivir exposures at 100 mg once daily and the occurrence of all lesions healed by Day 28. Cardiac Electrophysiology At 4 times the recommended maintenance pritelivir dose, clinically significant QTc interval prolongation was not observed.

sections.title: Pharmacokinetics
sections.text: The pharmacokinetic properties of pritelivir following oral administration of HOVILPRI are displayed in Table 2. Table 2: Pharmacokinetic Properties of Pritelivir Absorption Absolute bioavailability 72% T max , mean (range) a 3 h (2.0–4.5 h) Food effect b AUC ratio fed/fasted: 1.16 C max ratio fed/fasted: 1.33 Distribution Apparent volume of distribution (V d /F), geometric mean (%CV) c 64.1 L (37.3%) Plasma protein binding 97.3% Blood-to-plasma ratio, mean a AUC: 1.86 Metabolism Pritelivir is primarily metabolized by non- enzymatic hydrolysis to its major inactive metabolites, AIC090015 (26.3%) d and AIC090105 (14.4%) d Excretion % of dose excreted in urine e 76.4% (0.6% unchanged) % of dose excreted in feces e 15.5% (6.0% unchanged) Apparent clearance (CL/F), geometric mean (%CV) c 1.08 L/h (33.4%) Major route of elimination Non - enzymatic hydrolysis, followed by urinary excretion of the metabolites Half - life, mean a 60 h Steady - State Exposures f AUC 0-24 (μg•h/mL) 91.8 (49.0%) C max ( μ g/mL) 4.62 (50.7%) C trough ( μ g/mL) 3.14 (50.9%) a The values are based on a 100 mg once daily dose. b Food effect after high-fat meal: 150 calories from protein, 250 calories from carbohydrates, and 500-600 calories from fat; a total of 1000 calories with >50% calories from fat. c Derived from population pharmacokinetic model post-hoc estimates for all participants taking 20-280 mg single or multiple doses. d Percentages represent the molar ratio of each metabolite to total drug-related material in plasma. e Dosing in mass balance study: Healthy participants received pritelivir 500 mg (loading dose, Day 1) and 100 mg once daily (Days 2-8), with a [ 14 C]-labeled tracer dose co-administered on Day 8. Values represent recovery of total radioactivity as a percentage of administered dose. f Pharmacokinetic parameter values based on post-hoc estimates from pritelivir population pharmacokinetic model in immunocompromised participants receiving 100 mg of pritelivir once daily with or without food. Geometric mean (%CV). Abbreviations: T max , time to maximum plasma concentration; %CV, percent coefficient of variation; C max = maximum concentration; AUC 0-24 = area under the concentration-time curve over a dosing interval of 24 hours; C trough = concentration at the end of a dosing interval. C max and AUC were dose-proportional after single dose administration (20–480 mg) and multiple dose administration (5–400 mg once daily). After multiple dosing of 100 mg once daily, steady state was reached within 8 days. When a loading dose of 400 mg pritelivir was administered on Day 1 followed by a maintenance dose of 100 mg once daily, steady-state exposures were reached on Day 2. Plasma concentrations at steady state are approximately 5-fold higher than those after single dose administration. Specific Populations There were no clinically significant differences in the pharmacokinetics of pritelivir based on age (19 to 84 years), gender, race (including American Indian/Alaska Native, Asian, Black/African American, White, or other), body weight (48 to 176 kg), or underlying immunocompromised condition (including HIV/AIDS, oncology, transplant, or autoimmune/inflammatory disorder). Patients with Renal Impairment In a single-dose pharmacokinetic study, pritelivir exposure (AUC and C max ) was comparable between participants with mild (eGFR 60–89 mL/min) or moderate (eGFR 30–59 mL/min) renal impairment and those with normal renal function (eGFR ≥90 mL/min) . Pritelivir exposure (AUC and C max ) were approximately 1.6- fold higher in participants with severe renal impairment (eGFR 15–29 mL/min, not on hemodialysis) relative to those with normal renal function. Pritelivir pharmacokinetics in patients on hemodialysis is unknown. Patients with Hepatic Impairment In a single-dose pharmacokinetic study, pritelivir exposure (AUC and C max ) was comparable in participants with moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class B) relative to those with normal hepatic function. The effect of severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C) on pritelivir pharmacokinetics is unknown. Drug Interactions Clinical Drug Interaction Studies Effect of Other Drugs on the Pharmacokinetics of Pritelivir Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs): Co-administration of a single oral dose of 100 mg pritelivir (on Day 1) with esomeprazole 40 mg once daily (from Day -3 to Day 1; 4 days total) decreased C max by approximately 76% and AUC by approximately 59% compared to pritelivir administered alone [see Dosage and Administration (2.2), Warnings and Precautions (5.1), Drug Interactions (7.2)] . In the Phase 3 trial (PRIOH-1, Parts C-F), pritelivir exposures were evaluated for participants who received concomitant omeprazole or lansoprazole (≤20 mg daily), pantoprazole (≤40 mg daily), or an H2 -receptor antagonist (with pritelivir administered at least 2 hours before or 12 hours after the H2-receptor antagonist). Pritelivir exposures in participants receiving these acid-reducing agents were not clinically meaningfully different from those in participants who did not receive any acid-reducing agents [see Dosage and Administration (2.2), Warnings and Precautions (5.1), Drug Interactions (7.2)] . Table 3 : Changes in Pharmacokinetics of Pritelivir in the Presence of Co-administered Drugs Co - administered Drug and Regimen Pritelivir Regimen N Geometric Mean Ratio (90% CI) of Pritelivir Pharmacokinetics with/without Co-administered Drug (No Effect=1) AUC 0-inf AUC 0-last C max Esomeprazole 40 mg once daily 100 mg single dose 15 0.41 ( 0.36 , 0.48 ) 0.41 ( 0.35 , 0.47 ) 0.24 ( 0.20 - 0.30 ) Abbreviations: N=number of participants included in the pharmacokinetic analysis, CI= confidence interval, AUC= area under the concentration- time curve, C max = maximum concentration Effect of Pritelivir on the Pharmacokinetics of Other Drugs BCRP substrates: Co-administration of multiple pritelivir doses (400 mg on Day 1 followed by 100 mg once daily on Day 2 and Day 3) with a single 20 mg oral dose of rosuvastatin (on Day 3) resulted in a 1.7-fold increase in C max and a 1.4-fold increase in AUC of rosuvastatin compared to rosuvastatin administered alone [see Drug Interactions (7.1)]. Table 4: Changes in Pharmacokinetics of Co-administered Drugs in the Presence of Pritelivir Co - administered Drug and Regimen Pritelivir Regimen N Geometric Mean Ratio (90% CI) of Co- administered Drug Pharmacokinetics with/without Pritelivir (No Effect=1) AUC 0 - inf AUC 0 - last C max Rosuvastatin 20 mg single dose 100 mg once daily 1 6 1.37 (1.27, 1.48) 1.41 (1.28, 1.56) 1.67 (1.45, 1.92) Abbreviations: N=number of participants included in the pharmacokinetic analysis, CI= confidence interval, AUC= area under the concentration- time curve, C max = maximum concentration CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP3A4, and OATP2B1 substrates: No clinically significant changes in substrate exposures were observed in clinical drug-drug interaction trials when pritelivir was co-administered with the cytochrome P450 (CYP)2B6 substrate bupropion, the CYP2C8 substrate repaglinide, the CYP2C9 substrate flurbiprofen, the CYP3A4 substrate midazolam, and the organic anion transporting polypeptide (OATP)2B1 substrate celiprolol. In Vitro Drug Interaction Studies CYP enzymes: As pritelivir is primarily metabolized by non-enzymatic hydrolysis, leading to the formation of AIC090015 and AIC090105, clinically relevant drug-drug interactions with pritelivir as a CYP enzyme substrate are not expected. Pritelivir does not inhibit CYP1A2, CYP2A6, CYP2B6, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP2E1, or CYP3A4/5 at clinically relevant exposures. Pritelivir does not cause clinically relevant induction of CYP1A2, CYP2C9, or CYP2C19. Pritelivir does not cause time-dependent inhibition of any CYP enzymes. Transporters: Pritelivir is a substrate of both P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and BCRP efflux transporters in vitro , but is not a substrate of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OATP2B1, organic cation transporter (OCT)1, or organic anion transporter (OAT)1. Because pritelivir has a high absolute oral bioavailability of 72%, co-administration of P- gp or BCRP inhibitors is not expected to impact the oral absorption of HOVILPRI to a clinically relevant extent. Pritelivir does not inhibit P-gp, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, multidrug and toxin extrusion protein (MATE)1, or MATE2-K at clinically relevant exposures. Metabolites: The major circulating metabolites of pritelivir, AIC090015 and AIC090105, are not expected to inhibit CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, or CYP3A4 to a clinically relevant extent. No clinically significant differences in the pharmacokinetics of OAT substrates are predicted when co- administered with HOVILPRI 100 mg once daily.

arms.label: Group 1
arms.description:
Subjects (32 male and female subjects) received 400 mg pritelivir on Day 1, 100 mg pritelivir from Day 2 to 6 and 400 mg pritelivir from Day 7 to 16.

Furthermore, these subjects received moxifloxacin matching placebo on the Days 2 and 17.

arms.label: Group 2a
arms.description:
Subjects (16 male and female subjects) received the respective amounts of tablets of matching pritelivir matching placebo on Day 1 to Day 16 in Group 2a as verum tablets in Group1.

Furthermore, these subjects received 400 mg moxifloxacin on Day 2 and moxifloxacin matching placebo on Day 17.

arms.label: Group 2b
arms.description:
Subjects (16 male and female subjects) received the respective amounts of tablets of matching pritelivir matching placebo on Day 1 to Day 16 in Group 2b as verum tablets in Group1.

Furthermore, these subjects received moxifloxacin matching placebo on Day 2 and 400 mg moxifloxacin on Day 17.
